summary_paragraph: A male patient was admitted with hyponatremia (sodium 116) following a fall and transfer from rehab, where routine labs revealed low sodium. He reported increased shortness of breath, bilateral upper extremity pain worsened by the fall, and mouth discomfort. He has a history of SIADH, chronic bronchitis, moderate aortic stenosis, hypertension, and chronic diastolic heart failure. He was managed with a 1.5L fluid restriction and salt tablets, resulting in gradual sodium improvement to 129. His breathing remained stable on room air, and bronchitis was managed with inhalers. Pain was controlled with acetaminophen, tramadol, and lidocaine patches. Hypertension was addressed by increasing valsartan to 160 mg daily. Mouth pain was treated with Gelclair, and itching with hydroxyzine. He remained stable, with no neurological complications, and was discharged to extended care with instructions to continue fluid restriction, salt supplementation, and follow-up on H. pylori testing, skin cancer, and other chronic conditions.
